text.p: Schering-Plough Corp Thursday said it expects the company's strong financial results to continue in 1997 and projected research and development expenditures to approach $810 million for the year.
The projected 1997 R&D expenditures, up slightly from an earlier estimate, would be 12 percent higher than the $723 million spent in 1996.

Remarking on anticipated 1997 results, Richard Jay Kogan, president and chief executive officer, said, "Schering-Plough is performing well, with our ethical pharmaceutical business achieving solid gains, our R&D programs advancing through internal efforts and new research and licensing agreements, and tight controls being maintained on expenses."
"For 1997, we expect Schering-Plough once again will deliver another year of good earnings growth, with the percentage increase for earnings per share coming in around the low- to mid-teens."
